GlobalPolicy.module-level-focus: Fast deterministic checks close to the module; Docker and OpenCode seams faked.
GlobalPolicy.wave-level-focus: Checks only merged surfaces touched by the current wave.
GlobalPolicy.phase-level-focus: Broader integration and regression confidence, including at least one gated live OpenCode run.
GlobalPolicy.autonomy-gate: Each shared module needs commands, scenarios, observable evidence, and wave/phase follow-up before long autonomous execution.
GlobalPolicy.redaction: Never log secrets, credentials, raw provider tokens, or sensitive payloads — in live logs or persisted traces.
GlobalPolicy.evidence-capture: Tests capture logs by attaching an in-memory pino transport (or a captured stream) and assert on structured fields and [Module][function][BLOCK_NAME] markers — never by scraping prose. Docker and the OpenCode SDK are replaced by narrow fakes at their adapter boundaries (M-SANDBOX, M-OPENCODE) so module-level checks stay deterministic and fast.
GlobalPolicy.forbidden-marker-policy: A "forbidden marker" assertion proves a branch did NOT run: e.g. the failure path must not emit BLOCK_PERSIST_RUN, and BLOCK_TEARDOWN must appear on every path. Treat a missing required marker or a present forbidden marker on a critical branch as a verification defect, not a flaky test.
GlobalPolicy.determinism-bounds: Agent output is non-deterministic and is NOT asserted by exact text. Determinism is asserted only on what the tool controls: RunTrace normalization (same events -> same RunTrace), persistence round-trips, config validation, redaction, scheduling bounds, and structural trace shape. Live-agent scenarios are gated phase-level only.
GlobalPolicy.retry-timeout-bounds: The engine does not retry a run automatically (a failed run is a recorded outcome, not a retry loop); max-fix-attempts-per-step=2 governs the fix loop, not run execution. Every run has a hard timeout; on timeout M-OPENCODE returns a partial-but-marked trace (OPENCODE_RUN_TIMEOUT) and the sandbox is still torn down.
GlobalPolicy.semantic-check-policy: Semantic (LLM-judge) evaluation is used only for optional qualitative comparison of agent behavior across runs (UC-003), always bounded by an explicit rubric over a structured trace. It is never used to gate module-level correctness, which stays on deterministic and trace assertions.

VF-001.NAME: SingleRunHappyPath
VF-001.scenario: An experiment with a given system prompt, model, and task prompt runs in an isolated sandbox and produces a trace.
VF-001.expected-outcome: A persisted run record with a complete behavior trace and a success status.

VF-002.NAME: ParallelIsolation
VF-002.scenario: Several experiments run concurrently in separate sandboxes.
VF-002.expected-outcome: N independent traces; no run observes or mutates another's filesystem or session; concurrency stays within the bound.

required-signals.trace-sequence: N distinct sandboxIds, no shared mounts

VF-003.NAME: NetworkVacuum
VF-003.scenario: A sandboxed run can reach only the allowlisted LLM endpoint; all other egress is denied.
VF-003.expected-outcome: LLM calls succeed; a probe to a non-allowlisted host fails.

VF-004.NAME: GuaranteedTeardown
VF-004.scenario: A run fails or times out mid-flight.
VF-004.expected-outcome: The sandbox container and volumes are torn down; no orphaned resources remain.

required-signals.trace-sequence: Teardown runs even on the failure path.

VF-005.NAME: DeterministicTrace
VF-005.scenario: The same raw OpenCode event sequence is normalized twice.
VF-005.expected-outcome: Identical RunTrace output; diffTraces of two identical traces reports no differences.

scenarios.scenario-1: A valid experiment definition parses into a typed object.
scenarios.scenario-2: Missing/invalid fields are rejected with CONFIG_INVALID_INPUT.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: Invalid input must not produce a partial ExperimentDefinition.

scenarios.scenario-1: Marker bindings (runId, sandboxId) appear in structured output.
scenarios.scenario-2: Secret-shaped fields are redacted and never appear verbatim.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: Redacted values must not appear in any emitted line.

V-M-LOGGER.phase-follow-up: Sampled log review for leaked secrets.

scenarios.scenario-1: A raw event sequence folds into a complete RunTrace (steps, tool-calls, tokens, timings, finalOutput).
scenarios.scenario-2: Normalizing the same events twice yields an identical RunTrace (determinism, VF-005).
scenarios.scenario-3: A malformed event surfaces TRACE_MALFORMED_EVENT without corrupting prior steps.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: RunTrace shape stays stable regardless of SDK event-shape churn (Risk-2).
required-trace-assertions.assertion-2: diffTraces of two identical traces reports no differences.

V-M-TRACE.wave-follow-up: OpenCode adapter feeds real events into normalizeEvents.

scenarios.scenario-1: A sandbox is provisioned and disposed cleanly (Docker faked).
scenarios.scenario-2: Provision failure surfaces SANDBOX_PROVISION_FAILED and leaves no resources.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: dispose() (BLOCK_TEARDOWN) runs on every path, including failure (Risk-3).
required-trace-assertions.assertion-2: On SANDBOX_PROVISION_FAILED, no container/volume handle is returned and no orphaned resource id is logged.

V-M-SANDBOX.wave-follow-up: Integration with M-OPENCODE running inside the sandbox.
V-M-SANDBOX.phase-follow-up: Live VF-003 network-vacuum and VF-004 teardown checks.

scenarios.scenario-1: A faked SDK session streams events that M-TRACE folds into a complete RunTrace.
scenarios.scenario-2: A timeout surfaces OPENCODE_RUN_TIMEOUT with a partial-but-marked trace.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: Adapter is the only SDK-aware surface; event-shape divergence triggers replan, not a RunTrace patch (Risk-2).
required-trace-assertions.assertion-2: On OPENCODE_START_FAILED, BLOCK_STREAM_TRACE must NOT be emitted (no trace from a server that never started).
required-trace-assertions.assertion-3: On OPENCODE_RUN_TIMEOUT, the returned RunTrace is marked partial and carries the steps captured before the deadline.

V-M-OPENCODE.wave-follow-up: Engine persists the produced RunTrace via M-STORE.
V-M-OPENCODE.phase-follow-up: Gated live single run against a real OpenCode sandbox.

scenarios.scenario-1: A saved run round-trips through getRun and appears in listRuns.
scenarios.scenario-2: getRun on an unknown id surfaces STORE_NOT_FOUND.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: Persisted traces contain no redacted/secret values.

scenarios.scenario-1: A single experiment runs end to end (deps faked) and is persisted.
scenarios.scenario-2: N experiments run within the concurrency bound, each isolated.
scenarios.scenario-3: A failing run does not abort sibling runs and still tears its sandbox down.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: Concurrency never exceeds the configured bound (observe max concurrent BLOCK_SCHEDULE_RUNS in flight).
required-trace-assertions.assertion-2: Every scheduled run reaches a terminal state and emits a teardown ([Sandbox][createSandbox][BLOCK_TEARDOWN]) exactly once.
required-trace-assertions.assertion-3: A single run's failure must NOT prevent sibling runs from reaching BLOCK_PERSIST_RUN (no cross-run abort).
required-trace-assertions.assertion-4: A run that failed before completion must NOT emit BLOCK_PERSIST_RUN with status=success.

V-M-ENGINE.wave-follow-up: CLI dispatches into the engine unchanged.
V-M-ENGINE.phase-follow-up: VF-001, VF-002, VF-004 end to end.

scenarios.scenario-1: run/list/show/compare dispatch to the engine and emit parseable JSON with exit code 0.
scenarios.scenario-2: Bad usage emits CLI_BAD_USAGE and a non-zero exit code.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: stdout is machine-parseable so agents can consume results.

Gate-Phase-1.goal: Foundation modules have deterministic local checks with faked Docker/OpenCode seams and basic observability.

required-evidence.evidence-1: M-CONFIG, M-LOGGER, M-TRACE, M-SANDBOX, M-OPENCODE, M-STORE have module-local checks defined and passing.
required-evidence.evidence-2: Redaction verified: no secret leaks in logs or traces.

Gate-Phase-2.goal: End-to-end single and parallel runs work with bounded concurrency and guaranteed teardown.

required-evidence.evidence-1: VF-001 single-run and VF-002 parallel-isolation pass.
required-evidence.evidence-2: VF-003 network-vacuum and VF-004 teardown pass against a real sandbox (gated).

AutonomyReadiness.M-CONFIG: Pure validation; deterministic asserts cover success + failure; no external surface.
AutonomyReadiness.M-LOGGER: Redaction asserted by absence of secret values in captured output; no external surface.
AutonomyReadiness.M-TRACE: Pure functions; determinism (VF-005) and malformed-event handling are deterministic asserts.
AutonomyReadiness.M-SANDBOX: Module-local checks run against a Docker fake. Network-vacuum (VF-003) and teardown-on-crash (VF-004) require a gated live phase-level run before this module is trusted unattended.
AutonomyReadiness.M-OPENCODE: SDK faked at module level; real event-shape only proven by a gated live single run. Pre-1.0 SDK is the main replan risk.
AutonomyReadiness.M-STORE: Round-trip and not-found are deterministic; persisted-trace redaction asserted.
AutonomyReadiness.M-ENGINE: Orchestration/parallelism/isolation provable with fakes; final confidence needs VF-001/VF-002/VF-004 end to end at phase level.
AutonomyReadiness.M-CLI: Thin dispatch; parseable-stdout and exit-code contracts are deterministic.
AutonomyReadiness.required-packet-fields: module-id, write-scope, contract-excerpt, verification-excerpt, dependency-contract-summaries, stop-conditions, retry-budget — as in docs/operational-packets.xml ExecutionPacket.
AutonomyReadiness.required-checkpoint-fields: assumptions-kept, commands-run, evidence-captured, next-action — as in docs/operational-packets.xml CheckpointReport.
AutonomyReadiness.gap: No live OpenCode/Docker integration evidence exists until Phase-2 gated runs; the three "conditional" modules must not be marked phase-done on faked evidence alone.

packet-template.expected-fields: scenario, contract-ref, expected-evidence, observed-evidence, first-divergent-block, suggested-next-action
